verses.text: This is what the LORD says: "Look, I am going to stir up a destroying wind against Babylon and against the people of Leb Kamai.
I will send foreigners to Babylon to scatter her like chaff in the wind. They will strip her land bare. They will attack her from every side on her day of disaster.
Do not let her archers string their bows or put on their armor. Do not spare her young men. Completely destroy her army.
They will fall dead in the land of the Babylonians, stabbed through in her streets.
For Israel and Judah have not been abandoned by their God, the LORD of Armies, even though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.
Run away from Babylon! Run for your lives! Do not be destroyed because of her sins. It is time for the LORD's revenge. He will pay her back for what she has done.
Babylon was a gold cup in the LORD's hand. She made the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine, and so they have gone mad.
Babylon has suddenly fallen and been shattered. Wail for her! Get healing balm for her pain. Maybe she can be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Let us leave her and each go back to our own land. For her judgment reaches up to the heavens. It rises as high as the clouds.
The LORD has shown that we are in the right. Come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has done.
Sharpen the arrows! Pick up the shields! The LORD has stirred up the kings of the Medes, because he plans to destroy Babylon. This is the LORD's revenge, revenge for his temple.

Raise a flag against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the guard! Post the watchmen! Set up an ambush! For the LORD will do what he planned. He will carry out what he said he would do to the people of Babylon.
You who live beside many waters and are rich with treasures, your end has come. Your life is cut off like a thread.
The LORD of Armies has sworn by himself: 'I will surely fill you with soldiers like a swarm of locusts, and they will shout in victory over you.'
God made the earth by his power. He set the world in place by his wisdom. By his understanding he stretched out the heavens.
When he speaks, the waters in the heavens roar. He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Everyone is foolish and without knowledge. Every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols. His metal images are a lie. There is no breath in them.
They are worthless, objects of mockery. When the time comes to punish them, they will be destroyed.
But God, who is Jacob's portion, is not like them. He made everything, including Israel, the people who belong to him. The LORD of Armies is his name.
You are my war club, my weapon for battle. With you I smash nations. With you I destroy kingdoms.
With you I smash the horse and its rider.
With you I smash the chariot and its driver. With you I smash men and women. With you I smash the old and the young. With you I smash young men and young women.
With you I smash the shepherd and his flock. With you I smash the farmer and his oxen. With you I smash governors and officials.
Before your eyes I will pay back Babylon and all who live in Babylonia for all the evil they have done in Zion," says the LORD.

"Look, I am against you, you destroying mountain, you who destroy the whole earth," says the LORD. "I will stretch out my hand against you. I will roll you off the cliffs and make you a burned-out mountain.
No one will take even a stone from you for a cornerstone or a foundation. You will be a ruin forever," says the LORD.

"Raise a flag in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Get the nations ready to fight against her. Call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz to attack her. Appoint a commander against her. Send the horses like a swarm of locusts.
Get the nations ready to fight against her: the kings of the Medes, their governors and officials, and all the lands they rule.
The land shakes and twists in pain, because the LORD's plans against Babylon stand firm. He will make the land of Babylon a ruin where no one lives.
Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting. They stay in their fortresses. Their strength is gone. They have become as weak as women. Her homes are set on fire. The bars of her gates are broken.
One runner after another, one messenger after another, comes to tell the king of Babylon that his whole city has been captured.
The river crossings have been seized, the marshes set on fire, and the soldiers are terrified."
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled. Soon the time of harvest will come for her."
"Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured us and crushed us. He has emptied us like a jar. Like a monster he has swallowed us. He has filled his stomach with our best things, and then spit us out.
May Babylon pay for the violence done to us and to our families," say the people of Zion. "May the people of Babylonia pay for the blood they shed," says Jerusalem.
So this is what the LORD says: "Look, I will defend your case and take revenge for you. I will dry up her sea and make her springs run dry.
Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a home for jackals, an object of horror and mockery, a place where no one lives.
Her people will roar together like young lions. They will growl like lion cubs.
While they are excited, I will set out a feast for them and make them drunk, so that they shout with laughter. Then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up," says the LORD.
"I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams and goats.
How Sheshach has been captured, the pride of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a ruin among the nations!
The sea has risen over Babylon. Its roaring waves have covered her.
Her towns have become ruins, a dry land and a desert, a land where no one lives and no one travels through.
I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spit out what he has swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him. Even the wall of Babylon will fall.
Come out of her, my people! Run for your lives! Run from the LORD's fierce anger.
Do not lose heart or be afraid when you hear rumors in the land. One rumor comes this year, another the next. There will be rumors of violence in the land, of one ruler fighting another.
For look, the days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her dead will lie in the middle of her.
Then heaven and earth and everything in them will shout for joy over Babylon, because destroyers will attack her from the north," says the LORD.
"Babylon must fall because of the people of Israel she killed, just as the dead all over the earth fell because of Babylon.
You who have escaped the sword, go! Do not wait! Remember the LORD in a faraway land, and think about Jerusalem."
"We are ashamed because we have been insulted. Our faces are covered with disgrace, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD's temple."
"So look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will punish her idols. Throughout her land the wounded will groan.
Even if Babylon climbs up to the heavens and builds her fortress high and strong, I will still send destroyers against her," says the LORD.
"Listen! A cry comes from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Babylonians.
For the LORD is destroying Babylon and silencing her loud noise. The enemy comes like roaring waves, like crashing waters. Their battle cry rings out.
The destroyer has come against Babylon. Her warriors are captured, and their bows are broken. For the LORD is a God who pays people back. He will pay back in full.
I will make her officials and wise men, her governors, officials, and warriors drunk. They will fall asleep forever and never wake up," says the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.

This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Babylon's thick walls will be completely torn down, and her high gates will be burned. The nations wear themselves out for nothing. Their hard work only feeds the fire."

This is the message Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when Seraiah went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the officer in charge of the king's travel arrangements.
Jeremiah had written on a scroll all the disasters that would come on Babylon, all these words written about Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, make sure you read all these words out loud.
Then say, 'LORD, you have said you will destroy this place so that no one will live in it, neither people nor animals. It will be a ruin forever.'
When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates River.
Then say, 'In the same way Babylon will sink and never rise again, because of the disaster I will bring on her. Her people will wear themselves out.'" This is the end of Jeremiah's words.
